review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

2:1.sourceText: Θέλω γὰρ ὑμᾶς εἰδέναι ἡλίκον ἀγῶνα ἔχω ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν καὶ τῶν ἐν Λαοδικίᾳ καὶ ὅσοι οὐχ ἑόρακαν τὸ πρόσωπόν μου ἐν σαρκί,
2:1.targetText: For I wish you to know how great a conflict I have for you and those in Laodicea, and as many as have not seen my face in the flesh,

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately rendered in this English possessive or proper-name phrase.

2:2.sourceText: ἵνα παρακληθῶσιν αἱ καρδίαι αὐτῶν, συνβιβασθέντες ἐν ἀγάπῃ καὶ εἰς πᾶν πλοῦτος τῆς πληροφορίας τῆς συνέσεως, εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν τοῦ μυστηρίου τοῦ Θεοῦ, Χριστοῦ,
2:2.targetText: that their hearts may be comforted, being united in love, and to all riches of the full assurance of the understanding, to the full knowledge of the secret of the God and Father, and of the Christ,

groups.note: Christ is a shared lexical name; N1904 Χριστοῦ apposition and the longer LSV/TR coordinated construction are not claimed to have identical syntax.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately rendered in this English possessive or proper-name phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness difference: LSV follows the longer God and Father and Christ construction (TR καὶ Πατρὸς καὶ); N1904 has Θεοῦ, Χριστοῦ without Father or these conjunctions.

2:3.sourceText: ἐν ᾧ εἰσιν πάντες οἱ θησαυροὶ τῆς σοφίας καὶ γνώσεως ἀπόκρυφοι.
2:3.targetText: in whom are all the treasures of the wisdom and the knowledge hid,

2:4.sourceText: Τοῦτο λέγω ἵνα μηδεὶς ὑμᾶς παραλογίζηται ἐν πιθανολογίᾳ.
2:4.targetText: and this I say, that no one may deceive you with enticing words,

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness difference: LSV starts and, corresponding to TR δέ; N1904 begins directly Τοῦτο λέγω.

2:5.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ καὶ τῇ σαρκὶ ἄπειμι, ἀλλὰ τῷ πνεύματι σὺν ὑμῖν εἰμι, χαίρων καὶ βλέπων ὑμῶν τὴν τάξιν καὶ τὸ στερέωμα τῆς εἰς Χριστὸν πίστεως ὑμῶν.
2:5.targetText: for if even in the flesh I am absent—yet in the spirit I am with you, rejoicing and beholding your order, and the steadfastness of your faith in regard to Christ;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately rendered in this English possessive or proper-name phrase.
Greek article is not separately rendered in this English possessive or proper-name phrase.

2:6.sourceText: Ὡς οὖν παρελάβετε τὸν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν τὸν Κύριον, ἐν αὐτῷ περιπατεῖτε,
2:6.targetText: as, then, you received Christ Jesus the LORD, walk in Him,

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately rendered in this English possessive or proper-name phrase.

2:7.sourceText: ἐρριζωμένοι καὶ ἐποικοδομούμενοι ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ βεβαιούμενοι τῇ πίστει καθὼς ἐδιδάχθητε, περισσεύοντες ἐν εὐχαριστίᾳ.
2:7.targetText: being rooted and built up in Him, and confirmed in the faith, as you were taught—abounding in it in thanksgiving.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness difference: LSV includes TR ἐν αὐτῇ (in it, referring to faith) before the separate thanksgiving phrase; N1904 has only ἐν εὐχαριστίᾳ, linked to in thanksgiving.

2:8.sourceText: Βλέπετε μή τις ὑμᾶς ἔσται ὁ συλαγωγῶν διὰ τῆς φιλοσοφίας καὶ κενῆς ἀπάτης κατὰ τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, κατὰ τὰ στοιχεῖα τοῦ κόσμου καὶ οὐ κατὰ Χριστόν·
2:8.targetText: See that no one will be carrying you away as spoil through philosophy and vain deceit, according to the tradition of men, according to the rudiments of the world, and not according to Christ,

groups.note: The periphrastic future ἔσται ὁ συλαγωγῶν is kept as a constituent will be carrying … away as spoil; the article is not made an independent carrying word.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article before philosophy has no separate English article.
Greek article before men has no separate English article.

unmappedTarget.reason: English complement/purpose marker supplied after See; N1904 directly uses μή τις, with no ὅτι/ἵνα token here.

2:9.sourceText: ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ κατοικεῖ πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα τῆς Θεότητος σωματικῶς,
2:9.targetText: because in Him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily,

2:10.sourceText: καὶ ἐστὲ ἐν αὐτῷ πεπληρωμένοι, ὅς ἐστιν ἡ κεφαλὴ πάσης ἀρχῆς καὶ ἐξουσίας,
2:10.targetText: and you are made full in Him, who is the head of all principality and authority,

2:11.sourceText: ἐν ᾧ καὶ περιετμήθητε περιτομῇ ἀχειροποιήτῳ ἐν τῇ ἀπεκδύσει τοῦ σώματος τῆς σαρκός, ἐν τῇ περιτομῇ τοῦ Χριστοῦ,
2:11.targetText: in whom you also were circumcised with a circumcision not made with hands, in the putting off of the body of sins of the flesh by the circumcision of the Christ,

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness difference: LSV follows TR τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν (of sins) between body and flesh; N1904 has simply τοῦ σώματος τῆς σαρκός.

2:12.sourceText: συνταφέντες αὐτῷ ἐν τῷ βαπτίσματι, ἐν ᾧ καὶ συνηγέρθητε διὰ τῆς πίστεως τῆς ἐνεργείας τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ ἐγείραντος αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν·
2:12.targetText: being buried with Him in the immersion, in which you also rose with [Him] through the faith of the working of God, who raised Him out of the dead.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately rendered in this English possessive or proper-name phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English companion supplied for rose with; the syn-prefix conveys together/with, but no separate αὐτῷ is written with this second verb. The earlier actual αὐτῷ belongs to buried with Him.

2:13.sourceText: καὶ ὑμᾶς νεκροὺς ὄντας τοῖς παραπτώμασιν καὶ τῇ ἀκροβυστίᾳ τῆς σαρκὸς ὑμῶν, συνεζωοποίησεν ὑμᾶς σὺν αὐτῷ, χαρισάμενος ἡμῖν πάντα τὰ παραπτώματα,
2:13.targetText: And you—being dead in the trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh—He made alive together with Him, having forgiven you all the trespasses,

groups.note: The two N1904 accusative ὑμᾶς tokens restate the same object of made alive; LSV expresses this object once in its initial you. Neither token is wrongly moved to the later forgiven you, whose source person differs.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately rendered in this English possessive or proper-name phrase.
Source-witness person difference: N1904 ἡμῖν means to us, first person; LSV you follows TR ὑμῖν, second person.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness person difference: LSV having forgiven you is second person (TR ὑμῖν), not N1904 ἡμῖν (us).

2:14.sourceText: ἐξαλείψας τὸ καθ’ ἡμῶν χειρόγραφον τοῖς δόγμασιν ὃ ἦν ὑπεναντίον ἡμῖν, καὶ αὐτὸ ἦρκεν ἐκ τοῦ μέσου, προσηλώσας αὐτὸ τῷ σταυρῷ·
2:14.targetText: having blotted out the handwriting in the ordinances that is against us, that was contrary to us, and He has taken it out of the way, having nailed it to the Cross;

unmappedTarget.reason: English relative/copula expansion of attributive καθ’ ἡμῶν (against us); no corresponding relative pronoun or finite copula occurs in that first Greek phrase.

2:15.sourceText: ἀπεκδυσάμενος τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας ἐδειγμάτισεν ἐν παρρησίᾳ, θριαμβεύσας αὐτοὺς ἐν αὐτῷ.
2:15.targetText: having stripped the principalities and the authorities, He made a show of them openly—having triumphed over them by it.

unmappedTarget.reason: English object pronoun supplied after made a show of, referring back to the principalities and authorities. The actual αὐτούς accompanies the later triumphing verb and is linked to the second them.

2:16.sourceText: Μὴ οὖν τις ὑμᾶς κρινέτω ἐν βρώσει καὶ ἐν πόσει ἢ ἐν μέρει ἑορτῆς ἢ νεομηνίας ἢ σαββάτων,
2:16.targetText: Let no one, then, judge you in eating or in drinking, or in respect of a celebration, or of a new moon, or of Sabbaths,

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness conjunction difference: N1904 καί (and) joins eating and drinking; LSV or follows TR ἤ.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness conjunction difference: LSV eating or drinking corresponds to TR ἤ, whereas N1904 has καί (and).

2:17.sourceText: ἅ ἐστιν σκιὰ τῶν μελλόντων, τὸ δὲ σῶμα τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
2:17.targetText: which are a shadow of the coming things, but the body [is] of the Christ;

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

2:18.sourceText: μηδεὶς ὑμᾶς καταβραβευέτω θέλων ἐν ταπεινοφροσύνῃ καὶ θρησκείᾳ τῶν ἀγγέλων, ἃ ἑόρακεν ἐμβατεύων, εἰκῇ φυσιούμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ νοὸς τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ,
2:18.targetText: let no one deceive you of your prize, delighting in humble-mindedness and [in] worship of the messengers, intruding into the things he has not seen, being vainly puffed up by the mind of his flesh,

groups.note: καταβραβευέτω with its actual object ὑμᾶς is the idiom deprive/disqualify someone of the prize. The complete deceive you of your prize phrase is linked as a verbal constituent; no separate Greek prize noun is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately rendered in this English possessive or proper-name phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV supplies the repeated preposition for the coordinated worship phrase; only one ἐν is written before humility in Greek.
Source-witness polarity difference: LSV follows TR ἃ μὴ ἑώρακεν (things he has not seen); N1904 has positive ἃ ἑόρακεν.

2:19.sourceText: καὶ οὐ κρατῶν τὴν Κεφαλήν, ἐξ οὗ πᾶν τὸ σῶμα διὰ τῶν ἁφῶν καὶ συνδέσμων ἐπιχορηγούμενον καὶ συνβιβαζόμενον αὔξει τὴν αὔξησιν τοῦ Θεοῦ.
2:19.targetText: and not holding the Head, from which all the body—gathering supply through the joints and bands, and being knit together—may increase with the increase of God.

groups.note: N1904 ἐπιχορηγούμενον is a passive supplied/supported participle; LSV gives the receptive process as gathering supply. This is a contextual phrase correspondence, not an active/passive parsing claim.
N1904 αὔξει is present indicative (increases); LSV renders may increase. The lexical verb is shared; the English modal is not a Greek subjunctive form.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately rendered in this English possessive or proper-name phrase.

2:20.sourceText: Εἰ ἀπεθάνετε σὺν Χριστῷ ἀπὸ τῶν στοιχείων τοῦ κόσμου, τί ὡς ζῶντες ἐν κόσμῳ δογματίζεσθε
2:20.targetText: If, then, you died with the Christ from the rudiments of the world, why, as living in the world, are you subject to ordinances—

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness difference: LSV includes then, as TR οὖν; N1904 directly has Εἰ ἀπεθάνετε without the conjunction.

2:21.sourceText: Μὴ ἅψῃ μηδὲ γεύσῃ μηδὲ θίγῃς,
2:21.targetText: you may not touch, nor taste, nor handle—

2:22.sourceText: ἅ ἐστιν πάντα εἰς φθορὰν τῇ ἀποχρήσει, κατὰ τὰ ἐντάλματα καὶ διδασκαλίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων;
2:22.targetText: which are all for destruction with the using, after the commands and teachings of men,

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article before men has no separate English article.

2:23.sourceText: ἅτινά ἐστιν λόγον μὲν ἔχοντα σοφίας ἐν ἐθελοθρησκίᾳ καὶ ταπεινοφροσύνῃ καὶ ἀφειδίᾳ σώματος, οὐκ ἐν τιμῇ τινι πρὸς πλησμονὴν τῆς σαρκός.
2:23.targetText: which are, indeed, having a matter of wisdom in self-willed religion, and humble-mindedness, and neglecting of body—not of any value to satisfying the flesh.
